llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill does perform file reads/writes and network requests, but those capabilities are central to syncing provider configuration and are described in the docs; missing manifest permission declarations are a review-quality concern rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[TP4] expected: Endpoint probing, provider.api mutation, alias pruning, and caching are real, but the artifact documents dry-run/apply behavior, alias pruning, probe parameters, separate restart, and cache redaction. I did not find deceptive or automatic unrelated side effects.
[SDI-1] expected: The agents.defaults.models alias addition and pruning path is real and behavior-affecting, but it is explicitly disclosed as the v2 default, summarized as changes, and can be disabled with documented flags.
[SDI-2] expected: Live POST probes to /responses or /chat/completions are present and can use configured credentials, but they are optional probe modes for compatibility testing rather than default hidden execution.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The --allow-outside-provider escape hatch can broaden writes beyond the provider subtree when combined with a custom mapping. It is blocked by default and requires explicit invocation, so it warrants caution but does not make the normal skill behavior Review-worthy.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger examples are broader than the literal /provider_sync command, but they remain provider-sync or probe-oriented and the documented write path is framed around dry-run and confirmation.
llm.guidance: Install only if you want a tool that can modify OpenClaw provider configuration. Run dry-run first, review added/removed models and alias pruning, avoid provider=all or mode=apply unless intentional, use API keys only in trusted private contexts, and avoid custom mappings with --allow-outside-provider unless you fully understand every config path being written.
llm.summary: This skill appears to do what it says: sync provider model lists into OpenClaw configuration, with disclosed dry-run, apply, backup, alias-sync, and optional probing behavior.
